source.version: Web application without a public build: record the capture date, the account type (personal or Workspace, never the address) and the page format
source.copyBrowser: Copy in Google Docs and paste in the same browser: Google Docs writes the clipboard from inside the page, so each browser is its own source path

editor.adapt: The same address with formatting=adapt. A scenario with an editorQuery adds it to both addresses.
editor.images: No allowRemoteImages and no imageAssets: an image that Google Docs serves by URL is removed with image-removed and its alt text stays in its place; a data image within the bounds would be kept, which is a finding
editor.lineHeight: The default schema has no LineHeight: in preserve, the line spacing Google Docs writes on every paragraph is reported as destination-formatting-unconfirmed, and that warning shows the notice; adapt removes the spacing as an informational finding. A quiet scenario allows the warning in preserve, so its notice stays hidden only in adapt or when no pasted paragraph carries line spacing
editor.lineBreaks: Google Docs may write a br between blocks, after a table or for an empty paragraph. The editor makes one paragraph of line breaks from each run of them; the check ignores empty blocks a scenario does not name, and gdocs-empty-paragraphs reports a run that arrives as fewer empty paragraphs

conventions: This is an offline edited English regression specification. Block IDs and v1 document names remain stable. No native recapture was performed; baseline application instructions describe the shape being modeled.
Every paragraph starts with its block identifier, so any output order, loss or duplication is visible.

Create each document as a new Google Docs document with the title given here. Never create one by uploading or importing a .docx, .odt or .html file: that would capture a third party conversion. The large document is the one exception, pasted from a local browser tab as its blocks describe.

Before entering text, turn off Tools > Preferences > Automatically capitalize words, Use smart quotes and Automatic substitution. Copy each text from this file and paste it with Paste without formatting (Cmd+Shift+V), then apply the formatting named in docs.
A marker in list.docsLabel is what Google Docs shows. Do not type it; Google Docs creates it from the list formatting.

Images come from content/google-docs-images.mjs. Insert them only with Insert > Image > Upload from computer, never by URL, from Drive, Photos or a search, and give each the alt text named here (Cmd+Option+Y).
Keep the defaults of a new document: Pages format, Normal text in Arial 11 pt. Add no comments, suggestions, people, smart chips, bookmarks or headers.
Copy and paste in the same browser, and record the scenario's selection exactly.

documents.title: gdocs-v1-large
documents.docs: Open /private/tmp/large-v1.html in a browser tab, Select All, Copy, and paste it into the new document with Cmd+V so Google Docs keeps headings, lists and tables. Every capture copies only from the Google document.

blocks.description: Headings, paragraphs, bulleted and numbered lists and tables, 10,000 words, every block starting with consecutive tokens from G00001

scenarios.selection: GB01 to GB04: drag from the start of GB01 to the end of GB04

expected.preserve: GB01, GB02 and GB03 as headings of levels 1, 2 and 3 and GB04 as a paragraph, in that order. The Google Docs fonts, sizes and colors stay as text styles (GB04 in Arial 11 pt). Paragraph spacing is dropped without a finding; the line spacing on every paragraph is reported as destination-formatting-unconfirmed.
expected.adapt: The same blocks and heading levels without font, size, color or line spacing. Only informational formatting-adapted findings, so no notice.

expected.preserve: One paragraph, GB04, in Arial 11 pt; its line spacing is reported as destination-formatting-unconfirmed.
expected.adapt: The same paragraph without text styles; no notice.

expected.preserve: GB05 as a heading of level 2, then GB06 and GB07 as paragraphs with every diacritic, quote, apostrophe, dash and ellipsis exactly as in this file. Text styles stay; line spacing is reported as destination-formatting-unconfirmed.
expected.adapt: The same text without text styles; no notice.

expected.preserve: GB09 as one paragraph: bold bold, italic italic, underlined underlined and all three bold, italic and underlined, all as semantic marks. Line spacing is reported as destination-formatting-unconfirmed.
expected.adapt: The same marks without text styles; no notice.

expected.preserve: GB10: strikethrough struck through, the first 2 subscript, the second 2 superscript, Georgia in Georgia 14 pt, red in #ff0000 and highlighted highlighted. The full schema has Subscript, Superscript and LineHeight, so the line spacing raises no finding. Google Docs may size the subscript and superscript relative to their run, for example 0.6em; cleanup resolves that to an absolute size, 6.6pt in an 11 pt run, which stays as a text style without a finding. Record the shape and every finding.
expected.adapt: Strike, subscript and superscript stay; font, size, color and highlight are removed as informational formatting-adapted findings.

expected.preserve: GB11 as a heading of level 2; an example page linked to https://example.com/domternal/gdocs-v1, the GB13 address linked to itself and pisi@example.com linked to mailto:pisi@example.com. Google Docs styles link text with its own blue and an underline, so the link text also keeps an underline mark and the color #1155cc. No link-removed.
expected.adapt: The same links and underline marks without the blue; no notice.

expected.preserve: GB15 as a heading of level 3; GB16 centered, GB17 right aligned and GB18 justified; GB19's 1.5 spacing, like every Google Docs line spacing, is reported as destination-formatting-unconfirmed.
expected.adapt: The same blocks with default alignment and spacing; no notice.

expected.preserve: GB20 and GB21 as paragraphs without their indentation, reported as unsupported-formatting; the notice shows.
expected.adapt: The same: adapt does not remove indentation silently, so unsupported-formatting stays and the notice shows.

editedRegressionProvenance.method: Offline translation of authored prose and matching semantic text expectations, preserving structure, marks and intentional Unicode cases.
editedRegressionProvenance.baselinePolicy: Original sources and evidence remain preserved privately. This English variant is synthetic edited regression evidence, not a native Word or Google Docs capture.
editedRegressionProvenance.notesPolicy: Existing correction, provenance, capture, application instructions and observation descriptions explain the original source shapes or inherited expectations. They do not claim a new native observation of the English bytes.
